He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]]. ==High school career== McGowens played basketball for [[Wren High School]] in [[Piedmont, South Carolina]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 26.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, and three assists per game, and was named Region 1-4A Player of the Year. He led his team to a Class 4A Upper State runner-up finish.{{cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |title=Wren High basketball standout Bryce McGowens won't require surgery on wrist |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2019/02/23/bryce-mcgowens-wrist-injury-surgery-wren-high-ridge-view/2964687002/ |website=[[The Greenville News]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=February 23, 2019}} In his junior season, McGowens scored a school-record 65 points in a second-round win at the Class 4A playoffs.{{cite web |last=Preston |first=Geoff |title=Wren star and Florida State commit Bryce McGowens drops 65 points as Hurricanes advance |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/02/23/wren-basketball-and-fsu-commit-bryce-mcgowens-scores-65-hurricanes-advance-schsl-playoffs/4791334002/ |website=[[The Greenville News]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=February 23, 2020}} He averaged 25.3 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game as a junior, leading his team to the Class 4A Upper State championship game and repeating as Region 1-4A Player of the Year. For his senior season, McGowens moved to Legacy Early College in [[Greenville, South Carolina]].{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Kennington Lloyd III |date=April 20, 2020 |title=Top basketball prospect Bryce McGowens to transfer to Legacy Early College for senior year |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2020/04/20/wrens-bryce-mcgowens-transfer-legacy-early-college/5163155002/ |access-date=June 29, 2021 |website=[[Anderson Independent-Mail]]}} As a senior, he averaged 21.6 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game, earning South Carolina [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.{{cite web |last=Paniagua |first=Hunter |title=Husker recruit Bryce McGowens is South Carolina's Gatorade player of the year |url=https://omaha.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/husker-recruit-bryce-mcgowens-is-south-carolinas-gatorade-player-of-the-year/article_cfcedd5e-c54f-11eb-83db-4b4089cbc298.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=June 4, 2021}} He was selected to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] roster.{{cite web |title=Bryce McGowens – 2021–22 – Men's Basketball |url=https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2021-22/player/bryce-mcgowens |website=University of Nebraska Athletics |access-date=June 29, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== McGowens was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]]. On February 10, 2020, he announced his commitment to play college basketball for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Kennington Lloyd III |date=February 10, 2020 |title=Here's why Wren's Bryce McGowens picked Florida State over Clemson, Xavier and others |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2020/02/10/wren-four-star-bryce-mcgowens-commits-florida-state-basketball/4712499002/ |access-date=June 28, 2021 |website=[[Anderson Independent-Mail]]}} On October 8, 2020, McGowens decommitted from the program.{{cite web |last=Weiler |first=Curt |title=Five-star shooting guard Bryce McGowens decommits from Florida State |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2020/10/08/florida-state-fsu-basketball-recruiting-seminoles-bryce-mcgowens-decommit-five-star-leonard-hamilton/5923288002/ |website=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=October 8, 2020}} On November 13, 2020, he committed to [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]], becoming the highest-ranked recruit in program history and its first five-star recruit.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Bryce McGowens (No. 33) becomes Nebraska's highest-ranked commit |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30310425 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=November 13, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Basnett |first=Chris |title=Hoiberg says McGowens scored 25 points in a 75–74 loss to [[2021–22 Western Illinois Leathernecks men's basketball team|Western Illinois]] on November 9, 2021.{{cite news |title=Massner, Barisic rally Western Illinois past Nebraska 75–74 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372146 |access-date=November 16, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2021}} On March 1, 2022, he scored 26 points in a 78–70 win against [[2021–22 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] but suffered a hand injury that forced him to miss the following game against [[2021–22 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].{{cite news |last=Watkins |first=Jimmy |title=Nebraska's Bryce McGowens will miss Sunday's game at Wisconsin |url=https://omaha.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/nebraskas-bryce-mcgowens-will-miss-sunday-s-game-at-wisconsin/article_4e2dcde2-9d7f-11ec-8ad1-27027c9b6eb2.html |access-date=March 7, 2022 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 6, 2022}} McGowens was named third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] as well as to the All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2022|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} He averaged 16.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game. On March 21, 2022, McGowens declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Nebraska Cornhuskers freshman Bryce McGowens to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33564381 |access-date=March 21, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 21, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2022–2024)=== McGowens was selected with the 40th overall pick by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]] before being traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Draft Rights To No. 40 Pick Bryce McGowens From Minnesota Timberwolves|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-draft-rights-to-no-40-pick-bryce-mcgowens-from-minnesota-timberwolves|website=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=June 23, 2022}} On July 2, 2022, the Hornets announced that they had signed McGowens to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Bryce McGowens To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-bryce-mcgowens-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2022|access-date=July 2, 2022}} Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Hornets and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]]. On February 26, 2023, McGowens' deal was converted to a four-year, $7 million contract by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Bryce McGowens To Multi-Year Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-bryce-mcgowens-to-multi-year-deal|website=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2023|access-date=February 26, 2023}} McGowens was waived by the Hornets on July 6, 2024.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Davis Bertans, Bryce McGowens and Aleksej Pokusevski|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-davis-bertans-bryce-mcgowens-and-aleksej-pokusevski|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 12, 2024}} ===Portland Trail Blazers / Rip City Remix (2024–2025)=== On July 11, 2024, McGowens signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Bryce McGowens to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-bryce-mcgowens-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2024|access-date=July 12, 2024}} In 13 games for Portland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], he averaged 1.0 point, 0.2 rebounds, and 0.2 assists in 2.5 minutes per game. On March 26, 2025, while playing for the [[Rip City Remix]], McGowens suffered a season-ending right rib fracture.{{cite web | title=Bryce McGowens Injury Update | website=NBA | date=2025-03-26 | url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/bryce-mcgowens-injury-update | access-date=2025-12-06}} ===New Orleans Pelicans / Birmingham Squadron (2025–present)=== On July 30, 2025, McGowens signed a two-way contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans Sign Bryce McGowens To Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-bryce-mcgowens-to-two-way-contract|access-date=October 1, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On February 20, 2026, the Pelicans signed McGowens to a three-year, standard NBA contract worth $6.2 million.{{Cite web|title=Pelicans sign two-way guard Bryce McGowens to standard 3-year contract|url=https://www.fox8live.com/2026/02/20/pelicans-sign-two-way-guard-bryce-mcgowens-standard-3-year-contract/?outputType=amp|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=fox8live.com|language=en}} .403 || .274 || .831 || 5.2 || 1.4 || .7 || .3 || 16.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== McGowens' older brother, Trey, played college basketball for [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] before transferring to Nebraska.{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Kennington Lloyd III |date=November 20, 2020 |title=Brothers Bryce, Trey McGowens' lifelong dream will play out through Nebraska |access-date=June 29, 2021 |website=[[The Greenville News]]}} His father, Bobby, was a two-sport athlete in basketball and football at [[South Carolina State Bulldogs and Lady Bulldogs|South Carolina McGowens' mother, Pam, played basketball for [[Western Carolina Catamounts women's basketball|Western Carolina]].
